note: Authored scenario definitions are not executed results. Executed probes and their limits are in test/evals/RESULTS.md.

scenarios.title: Instanced particles collapse after moving to TSL
scenarios.query: We moved our InstancedMesh sphere particles to WebGPU and TSL. Now every sphere is a single dot. The material does material.positionNode = positions.element(instanceIndex). Fix it.
expected_behavior: Explains that positionNode replaces the position after skinning, morphs and instancing, so the sphere's own vertices are discarded
Fixes with positionLocal.add(positions.toAttribute()) or the equivalent, keeping the sphere geometry
Mentions the sprite pattern (SpriteNodeMaterial with positionNode = buffer.toAttribute() and count) as the alternative for point-like particles
Does not suggest computeAsync as a way to wait for the GPU

scenarios.title: A character that slides and snaps to T-pose
scenarios.query: Our glTF character's feet slide when running, and after the death animation it pops back into a T-pose. We use three.js r186 AnimationMixer.
expected_behavior: Sets clampWhenFinished = true and LoopOnce on the death action, explaining that a finished unclamped action disables itself
Derives run timeScale from actual movement speed over the clip's authored speed, and explains how to measure authored speed
Keeps locomotion clips in place and moves the character from code or physics; notes three.js has no built-in root motion
Listens for 'finished' on the mixer, not on the action

scenarios.title: Compress a heavy model for a drei scene
scenarios.query: This 80 MB GLB loads through drei useGLTF in our React Three Fiber app. Make it small with KTX2 and meshopt.
expected_behavior: Uses gltf-transform (etc1s/uastc for KTX2, meshopt) or a native gltfpack build; notes the npm gltfpack cannot compress textures
Notes KTX2 in gltf-transform needs the ktx CLI from KTX-Software 4.4 or newer, not toktx
Produces EXT_meshopt_compression, because drei's useGLTF (three-stdlib) does not read KHR_meshopt_compression
Validates before and after, keeps the raw file, and measures the result against a target profile or asks for one

scenarios.title: An enemy character on a machine with Asset Foundry
scenarios.query: We need a rigged enemy with idle, attack, hit and death clips for the web game. Asset Foundry is running on this machine.
expected_behavior: Detects the foundry_* tools or the asset-foundry skill and delegates the order instead of calling Meshy or Tripo directly
Supplies a target profile (skinning allowed, max influences 4, budgets) and the canonical clip names
Notes that provider preset names differ (no literal 'attack' or 'death' preset) and maps them to the canon
Runs its own acceptance check on the delivered file and records the manifest and licence

scenarios.title: A crowd of five thousand
scenarios.query: Show 5,000 animated people walking around a plaza in the browser, each at a different phase.
expected_behavior: Rules out BatchedMesh for skinned characters
Compares shared-pose skinned instancing, per-instance timing with compute skinning, and vertex-animation textures, with their costs
Recommends measuring the CPU cost of per-instance mixer.setTime and moving to VAT when it dominates
Adds reduced-motion and off-screen update policies

scenarios.title: A landing-page hero is not this pack's job
scenarios.query: Design the scroll-driven 3D particle hero for our marketing landing page.
expected_behavior: Routes the design of the hero and its scroll motion to sheleg-design
Offers web3d-runtime only for implementation questions the design raises (renderer, TSL, performance)
Does not invent a motion design itself
